raw.assessment: The incumbent provides free, repeatable conversational practice and printed access; seven frequent attendees explicitly valued its structure (H3-O6). Predictability may reduce their orientation burden, but this is a hypothesis. The concrete limiting observation is five occasional attendees struggling to enter conversations already familiar to partners (H3-O6): the same continuity may help some while hindering others. Slow pairing and partner changes suggest friction without establishing its cause (H3-O5). Available slips show 49/72 reporting sufficient useful practice and 48/72 identifying preparation correctly; missing and unlinked responses prevent a complete attendance-level assessment (H3-O2,O3,O7). Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes (H3-O4).

openings.claim: Unequal familiarity with the conversation, rather than proficiency mismatch alone, may explain some difficult pair starts.
openings.delta: Retain the valued session structure while testing whether a shared starting point improves entry for occasional attendees.
openings.prediction: Pairs using a fresh, self-contained prompt and brief mutual introduction will start reciprocal speaking sooner and report more useful practice, especially where prior topic familiarity differs.
openings.probe: Within a session, randomly offer consenting pairs either the usual prompt or a fresh self-contained equivalent with a one-minute introduction. Privately record topic familiarity without proficiency labels; anonymously observe time to reciprocal speaking and each partner's speaking minutes, then collect usefulness reports. Keep both activities inside 75 minutes and record volunteer preparation time.
assumptions: Equivalent prompts can be prepared within the weekly coordination ceiling.
Familiarity can be reported privately; unequal proficiency and prompt differences remain alternative explanations.

openings.claim: Some preparation errors may reflect confusion between current and earlier task information.
openings.delta: Test task identification at paper handoff before attributing errors to irregular attendance or motivation.
openings.prediction: A clearly dated paper card naming the next session and one preparation task will reduce earlier-task answers relative to the existing presentation.
openings.probe: Give consenting attendees the same next task in either existing format or a reusable dated-card format. Ask privately which task and session it refers to; correct every misunderstanding and provide the dated information to everyone afterward. Count earlier-task and blank answers separately and log printing, explanation, and message time.
assumptions: Immediate identification may not predict later recall.
The card is available without an account and does not make preparation a condition of participation.

raw.assessment: The supplied observations suggest difficulties with conversation entry and preparation continuity, but establish neither their causes nor the distribution of speaking time. Both capabilities below are hypotheses; neither is demonstrated to meet the six-session targets.

openings.claim: A self-calibrating conversation could let partners use different amounts of support while discussing the same fresh prompt, without declaring proficiency or relying on previous attendance.
openings.delta: Speculative capability: continuously adjust each person's conversational challenge. Dependencies: accessible entry prompts, independently usable scaffolds, turn allocation, and a reliable signal that challenge remains useful. Presently testable partial capability: reuse existing sheets with optional sentence starters and extension prompts; alternate speaker roles for two six-minute turns before jointly choosing whether to change support.
openings.prediction: If unequal entry difficulty or turn allocation contributes to low usefulness, the supported rounds should increase both partners' reported useful minutes and reduce the within-pair speaking-time gap. Unchanged usefulness despite more balanced speech would weaken that explanation.
openings.probe: Within a session, alternate the order of usual and supported rounds across pairs using comparable fresh prompts. Anonymous observation records each partner's speaking time; brief round slips record useful minutes and entry difficulty. Log preparation time and include it in weekly coordination totals.
assumptions: Scaffolds can be adapted within existing volunteer time.
Participants can select support without public proficiency labels.
Balanced speaking does not necessarily mean useful practice.

openings.claim: An attendance-independent preparation packet could make the next task recoverable after missed sessions through calendar dates alone.
openings.delta: Speculative capability: preserve preparation continuity without tracking learners. Dependencies: a stable six-session topic sequence, self-contained tasks, unambiguous dates, and printed distribution. Testable partial capability: provide six dated, detachable preparation cards made from existing topics, with spare packets available at every session.
openings.prediction: If stale task information contributes to errors, dated packets should specifically reduce naming an earlier task; persistent blank answers would suggest an additional barrier.
openings.probe: Ask participants to identify the next task using the current sheet and the dated packet, counterbalancing order. Record earlier-task errors separately from blanks. Then track task identification across six sessions, counting packet creation, printing and replacement effort toward the weekly 90-minute limit.
assumptions: Topics can be fixed six sessions ahead.
Participants retain packets or obtain a replacement.
No preparation or prior attendance becomes an entry requirement.

openings.claim: Unequal topic familiarity may impede conversation entry.
openings.discriminator: A shared fresh start speeds reciprocal speaking, especially across familiarity differences.
openings.fit: Preserves valued structure, label privacy and unrestricted attendance.
openings.probe: Randomize consenting pairs to usual versus equivalent fresh prompt plus one-minute introduction; privately record familiarity, observe individual speaking minutes and collect usefulness reports.
openings.uncertainty: Proficiency and prompt differences remain alternatives; preparation cost unknown.

openings.claim: Optional scaffolds and allocated turns may improve individual challenge and participation.
openings.discriminator: More balanced speech without greater usefulness weakens the proposed explanation.
openings.fit: Preserves conversation and private support selection.
openings.probe: Counterbalance usual and supported rounds using comparable fresh prompts, sentence starters, extensions and alternating six-minute roles; observe individual speech and collect usefulness and entry-difficulty slips.
openings.uncertainty: Continuous self-calibration is speculative; support and turn effects remain bundled; balanced speech need not be useful.

openings.claim: Dated information may resolve stale-task confusion; a six-session detachable packet additionally enables recovery after absence.
openings.discriminator: Earlier-task errors should decline; persistent blanks imply another barrier.
openings.fit: Printed, account-free access; preparation never required for entry.
openings.probe: Compare existing presentation with dated next-task card at handoff, correcting misunderstandings afterward. Separately counterbalance current sheet versus packet, then track identification across six sessions; provide spare packets and log creation, printing, replacement, explanation and message effort.
openings.uncertainty: Immediate identification may not predict recall; packet recovery depends on fixed topics and retention or replacement.

lineage.reason: Support and turn-allocation mechanism remains distinct.
Merged with A2; preserves immediate presentation test.
Merged with Z2; preserves absence recovery and packet dependencies.

post_distill.decision: Test as hypotheses only: synthetic, missing and unlinked reports establish no cause or success. Preserve free entry, no attendance or public-label requirements, 75 minutes, unpaid facilitation, offline information and conversational purpose. Log all volunteer effort; evaluate six-session targets of 80% useful practice, 85% task identification and under 90 coordination minutes weekly.
